text: A scam call can sound official, urgent, even caring. The danger begins when someone feels too frightened to hang up.
Meet Raksha. A second listener that spots the script, explains the pressure, and brings in someone you trust.
This is the working app at raksha app dot web dot app. No account is needed. We will start with a fictional digital arrest call.
The caller claims to be an officer. As each line arrives, Moss compares it with a playbook of scam tactics inside the server process.
Watch what happens when pressure turns into a request. Raksha raises a warning and shows why this conversation matches a scam pattern.
The most important part is simple: the exact words to say. I will not continue this call. I am going to verify this myself. Goodbye.
Now open the guardian link in a second tab. Someone you trust sees the same call, the same risk, and the words that triggered the warning.
The guardian can send a message through the shield, or ask what the caller requested. Moss searches only this call's context to find the relevant lines.
A useful shield must also know when to stay quiet. Here is a genuine hospital appointment call. It finishes without a danger alert.
We test complete conversations, including legitimate mentions of money and codes. A safe score means no recognised scam pattern, not verified identity.
The playbook makes retrieval visible. Type something a scammer might say and inspect the matching lines, tactics and similarity scores.
The latency lab runs real queries against the deployed app. It separates engine search, embedding plus search, and the browser round trip.
That distinction matters. Fast retrieval helps the warning arrive sooner, but network delay and speech recognition still affect the complete experience.
Moss handles the fast path. A deterministic risk engine decides when to warn. The language model adds coaching separately, so detection does not wait for it.
Firebase serves the clean public address. Cloud Run hosts the app and live sockets. Call memory stays in the server process and is scoped to each conversation.
Our committed evaluation caught all ten scripted scam calls and raised no danger alert on eight genuine calls. That is a starting point, not proof of real world accuracy.
Next come broader testing, more languages, stronger guardian invitations and on device speech. Raksha gives people a moment to pause before a scam becomes a loss.
